title: CTAB Extraction from Sample Ground in Liquid Nitrogen
author: Jordan Beasley
materials: Dispense some liquid nitrogen in a small dewer (small thermos size)
Quantify extract on Nanodrop and/or Qubit.

steps.title: Grind sample in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Fill a mortar with liquid nitrogen, let it boil off completely, add a small additional amount of liquid nitrogen, grind the frozen sample with a pestle to a fine powder, and scrape the powder into a 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Add CTAB, sarkosyl, Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl CTAB, 50 µl sarkosyl, and 50 µl Proteinase K to the powder, then vortex to mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Incubate at 60 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a hot block set to 60 °C and incubate either overnight or, if in a rush, for 60–90 minutes.

steps.title: Add phenol‑chloroform
steps.instruction: After incubation, add 300 µl phenol‑chloroform to the tube to extract DNA into the aqueous layer.

steps.title: Mix extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Mix by inversion on a rotator for 15 minutes if high‑molecular‑weight DNA is required; otherwise vortex well.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at 16 rpm (max speed) and label a new tube for the upcoming aqueous phase.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous layer
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the top aqueous layer without disturbing the white protein layer and transfer it to the newly labeled tube.

steps.title: Add SEVAC and mix
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl SEVAC to the transferred aqueous layer and mix by placing on a rotator for 15 minutes; alternatively vortex if high‑molecular‑weight DNA is not needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge SEVAC extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at 16 rpm (max speed) and label a new tube for the next transfer.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous layer after SEVAC
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the top aqueous layer, avoiding disturbance of the white protein layer, and transfer it to the newly labeled tube.

steps.title: Repeat centrifugation and transfer
steps.instruction: Repeat the centrifugation (3 minutes at 16 rpm max speed) and aqueous‑layer transfer step once more to ensure complete extraction.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 400 µl isopropanol to the aqueous solution and mix by inverting only (do NOT vortex); DNA may begin to precipitate.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 16 rpm (max speed); a visible pellet may form.

steps.title: Remove supernatant without disturbing pellet
steps.instruction: Remove as much of the liquid as possible without disturbing the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl 70 % ethanol to the pellet to wash away isopropanol and invert the tube several times to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge and remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 16 rpm (max speed) and remove as much ethanol as possible without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Dry pellet on hot block
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a hot block with the lid open at 60 °C for 5 minutes to evaporate any remaining ethanol.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in sterile water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 30–50 µl sterile water; flick the tube to aid dissolution and, if the pellet is stubborn, briefly return the tube to the 60 °C hot block.
